title: Implement region-aware KMS fallback proxy and RBAC v2 conditions cache
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Adds an RBAC v2 conditions cache to reduce policy-eval latency; introduces a region-aware KMS fallback proxy with audited failover events and rate-limited use. No customer-facing API changes, rollout via staged feature flag.
description:
Motivation: Large tenants and hot operator flows were causing repeated RBAC v2 policy evaluations and spiky latency in path checks; during rare primary KMS outages region-pinned tenants experienced hard failures rather than graceful fallbacks. This PR implements two coordinated mitigations: a local memory-backed 'conditions cache' for the policy-evaluator to amortize repeated condition computations, and a region-aware KMS fallback proxy that performs safe, auditable failovers to configured geo-fallback keys/providers when the primary KMS is unavailable.

What changed (summary):
- policy-evaluator/service: add conditions cache keyed by (policy_id, principal_digest, resource_hash, evaluation_window) with TTLs and stats; cache is invalidated on policy updates or principal claim changes.
- kms-proxy/service: new region-aware routing layer that picks primary KMS per tenant region pin, with configurable fallback chain (secondary provider, cross-region CMK) and a failover hysteresis/circuit-breaker to avoid cascading failovers.
- audit-proxy: enrich audit events with residency_evidence, kms_routing_decision, and fallback_reason fields when fallback occurs; emits a synthetic audit note for each fallback for downstream compliance ingestion.
- config & schema: add tenant.kms.fallback_chain and policy_evaluator.cache.* config knobs; feature flag rollout: feature.rbac.conditions_cache and feature.kms.geo_fallback.
- SDKs & tests: operator CLI now surfaces fallback metadata for diagnostic commands; added unit/integration tests and a small end-to-end scenario in the perf-canary suite.

Files changed (high level):
- services/policy-evaluator/src/cache.rs (new); services/policy-evaluator/src/evaluator.rs (cache hooks); services/policy-evaluator/config.yaml
- services/kms-proxy/src/router.rs (fallback chain); services/kms-proxy/src/health.rs (circuit-breaker); services/kms-proxy/config.schema.json
- services/audit-proxy/src/enricher.rs; docs/operator/diagnostics.md; infra/helm/values.kms-fallback.yaml
- tests/integration/kms_fallback_e2e.test; perf-canary/scenarios/region-fallback.yaml

Small illustrative snippet (conditions cache access pattern):
let key = ConditionsKey::new(policy_id, principal.digest(), resource.hash(), window_id);
if let Some(result) = cache.get(&key) { return result; }
let result = evaluate_conditions(...);
cache.insert(key, result.clone(), ttl_ms);
return result;

Testing and verification:
- unit tests for cache eviction and policy invalidation added (policy-evaluator).
- integration tests for kms-proxy simulate primary provider timeouts and assert fallback selection and audit enrichment.
- perf-canary has a staged test to confirm p95 policy-eval latency improvement under hotspot load (expected ~18-25% lower p95 after cache warmed).
- CI: lint, unit, integration; all checks passed in this branch after a re-run of flaky kms-proxy healthcheck test.

Rollout plan:
1) Merge behind feature flags (both flags default OFF).
2) Enable condition cache for 10% of traffic on a subset of tenants (feature.rbac.conditions_cache). Monitor policy-eval latency and cache hit rate.
3) Enable kms geo-fallback in read-only diagnostic mode (does not alter routing) and validate emitted audit events.
4) Gradually enable write-capable fallback for selected non-production tenants, with strict rate caps.
5) Full rollout when telemetry shows stable failure rates and no unexpected audit gaps.

Operational notes and safeguards:
- Fallback events generate a high-cardinality audit marker; downstream audit-ingestor has a sampling/aggregation rule to avoid overload.
- KMS fallback chain enforces tenant-level allowlist and per-tenant rate caps; the proxy refuses fallback outside configured policy.
- Cache invalidation is wired to the existing policy change webhook; an emergency flush endpoint was added to the policy-evaluator admin API.

Review conversation (high level):
- Liam Chen: "This looks good overall; please add metrics for cache hit/miss by tenant and a histogram for fallback latency."
- Asha (author): "Added cache.{hits,misses,entries} counters and kms_proxy.fallback_latency histogram. Also added a dashboard tile in observability-pack manifest."
- Sofia Morales: "Can we ensure fallback_reason is non-sensitive? auditors want structured, non-PHI strings."
- Asha: "Yes — fallback_reason is an enum token (PRIMARY_TIMEOUT|HEALTHCHECK_FAIL|RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED) and we redact any provider-specific IDs; added unit test."
- Marcus Lee: "Double-check helm values don't expose fallback chains for public tenants by default."
- Asha: "Default chart values have fallback disabled; updated README to call this out."
- Reviewer approvals: Liam (LGTM), Sofia (LGTM), Marcus (approved).

Related work: ENG-4982 (RBAC perf roadmap), SEC-332 (KMS failover security requirements), SUP-904 (customer report about region outage from Q4).

Notes on differences from previous PRs: this PR focuses on coordinated runtime-level resilience (caching + safe failovers) and audit enrichment rather than policy model changes or new RBAC types. The implementation prioritizes observable, auditable semantics for compliance rather than silent silent auto-fallback.

If there are follow-ups: planned items include a policy-driven fallback planner (allow tenants to opt in per-resource class), a deeper simulation harness for multi-region failover, and a migration guide for enterprise customers that want pre-provisioned cross-region fallback CMKs.
